name: Partial Cryptophthalmia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical diagnostic criteria for partial cryptophthalmia

criteria.description: Partial or incomplete fusion of the eyelids with absence of normal eyelid fissure
Malformation or absence of anterior segment ocular structures such as cornea and conjunctiva
Presence of associated orbital anomalies including microphthalmia or anophthalmia
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with cryptophthalmia (e.g., FOXE3 mutations)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of partial eyelid fusion with malformation of anterior ocular structures, confirmed clinically or by imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging and genetic testing when available.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Partial eyelid fusion with absent palpebral fissure
searchTerms: partly fused eyelids with no eye opening
missing eyelid opening due to fusion

pathognomonic.symptomName: Anterior segment ocular malformation including corneal agenesis
searchTerms: front eye defects including missing cornea
absent cornea and front eye abnormalities

common.symptomName: Visual impairment or blindness in affected eye
searchTerms: poor vision or blindness in one eye
loss of sight in affected eye

occasional.symptomName: Eyelid coloboma adjacent to fused area
searchTerms: eyelid defect adjacent to joined part

occasional.symptomName: Epiphora due to lacrimal drainage anomalies
searchTerms: watery eyes from blocked tear ducts

rare.symptomName: Associated systemic anomalies such as cleft lip or palate

laboratory: Genetic testing revealing mutations in FOXE3 or related ocular development genes
imaging: Orbital ultrasound or MRI showing absent or malformed anterior segment structures
CT scan demonstrating eyelid fusion and orbital hypoplasia
genetic: Other rare mutations affecting ocular morphogenesis genes
other: Clinical examination confirming partial eyelid fusion and ocular malformations

distinguishingFeatures: Complete eyelid fusion with total absence of palpebral fissure
Presence of ankyloblepharon (eyelid adhesion) rather than fusion
Associated ectodermal dysplasia and clefting anomalies

redFlags: Associated systemic malformations indicating syndromic involvement
references: OMIM Entry on Cryptophthalmia and FOXE3 mutations
Clinical Ophthalmology Reviews on congenital eyelid anomalies
